sections.h2: Which office mails the tax statement for a house in Tyler?
sections.html:
Smith County's tax office handles billing and collection for every local taxing unit in the county, Tyler included. The office is at 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, TX 75702, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 2011, and the number is (903) 590-2920.

Per the city, the counter opens at 8 a.m., closes at half past four and stays staffed through lunch. One Tyler bill can therefore carry several lines: the city, Smith County, Tyler Junior College and a school district. Which school district appears depends on the address, because the city notes that some Tyler properties sit in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD instead of Tyler ISD.

sections.h2: What are the Tyler property tax rates?
sections.html:
The City of Tyler's tax page prints the 2026-2027 rates as $0.242063 for the city, $0.374088 for Smith County, $0.210312 for Tyler Junior College and $0.835000 for Tyler ISD. Smith County's own rate table lists the same figures for tax year 2026 as adopted rates.

sections.h2: How has the Tyler city tax rate changed over time?
sections.html:
The city says it has cut its rate by more than 50 percent since the mid 1990s: its history table starts at $0.5336 for 1994-95 and reaches a low of $0.1990 in 2007-08. The rate then rose to $0.2699 in 2021-22 before dropping each year to $0.236452 in 2025-26.

The 2026-27 rate of $0.242063 is a step up from the prior year, and the same Smith County table shows the city's rate sitting above its no-new-revenue rate of 0.232965. The city also says it continues a two-cent commitment of its tax rate to the street fund, equal to $2.4 million.

  • 1994-95: $0.5336
  • 2007-08: $0.1990
  • 2021-22: $0.2699
  • 2025-26: $0.236452
  • 2026-27: $0.242063

sections.h2: How have other Tyler-area rates moved since 2022?
sections.html:
Smith County's rate table shows five years of adopted rates, and most Tyler-area lines fell from 2022 to 2026 while the county's rose.

  • Smith County: 0.330000 in 2022, 0.347264 in 2023, 0.364231 in 2024 and 2025, then 0.374088 in 2026.
  • Tyler ISD: 1.179300 in 2022, 0.960000 in 2023, 0.910000 in 2024, 0.845000 in 2025 and 0.835000 in 2026.
  • Tyler Junior College: 0.188001 in 2022, then 0.185068 in 2025 and 0.210312 in 2026.
  • City of Tyler: 0.261850 in 2022 and 0.242063 in 2026.

The table also prints each unit's voter-approval rate. For the city it equals the adopted figure of 0.242063 for 2026. Your own statement from the tax office controls, so use it for the exact figure.

sections.h2: What sales and lodging taxes apply in Tyler?
sections.html:
Tyler's sales tax rate is 8.25 percent, according to the city. That splits into 6.25 percent for the State of Texas, 1 percent for the city's general fund, 0.5 percent for Tyler's One Half Cent Sales Tax Corporation and 0.5 percent for Smith County.

Voters approved the half-cent corporation on November 7, 1995. The city says it brings in roughly $10.9 million a year for capital projects, including drainage and street work, Faulkner Park, the Glass Recreation Center and the airport terminal, which lets the city pay cash rather than issue general obligation bonds.

Hotel and motel occupancy tax and short-term rental tax are paid through the city's online portal at tylertx.hdlgov.com. This matters if you own a Tyler house that has been rented by the night: ask the city finance department about any unpaid occupancy tax before you list. The city's budget and tax rate hearings are held each August and September.

sections.h2: What is Tyler like for a seller?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures put Tyler at 113,723 people in mid 2025 across 57.45 square miles of land, a gain of 7.4 percent over the 2020 base. The city counts 38,505 households at 2.70 people each.

  • Middle owner-occupied home value, 2020-2024: $235,300.
  • Owners occupy 55.4 percent of Tyler homes.
  • Monthly cost of owning, with a loan: $1,743; with no loan: $664.
  • Median gross rent: $1,252.
  • Median household income: $67,486 (2024 dollars).

Retail sales in 2022 totaled about $4.84 billion, or $44,237 per resident.

sections.h2: When are Tyler property taxes due?
sections.html:
Texas bills go out around October 1 and payment is due on receipt, but the penalty-free window runs through January 31. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, according to the Comptroller.

Once delinquent, the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest, penalty grows one percent a month until July 1 when it reaches 12 percent, and interest keeps running at one percent a month. A taxing unit's attorney can add up to 20 percent more. Homeowners may qualify to split the bill: one payment by November 30 and the balance by June 30 of the next year, under the calendar the Comptroller publishes, which the Smith County office can confirm for your bill.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Tyler homeowner claim?
sections.html:
School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption under state law, and owners 65 and over or disabled receive another $60,000 off the school district value. The application deadline for most exemptions is before May 1 with the appraisal district.

Other state-level protections apply to Tyler homes too:

  • A 10 percent annual cap on appraised value increases for a residence homestead, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified.
  • A school-tax ceiling for seniors and disabled owners that can move with them to a new Texas homestead.
  • Disabled veteran exemptions of up to $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 depending on rating, and a total exemption for a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.

Cities, counties and colleges may adopt local exemptions, and the amounts for the City of Tyler, Smith County and Tyler Junior College are not printed on the pages above. Ask the Smith County Appraisal District for the current local percentages.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Tyler appraisal?
sections.html:
The appraisal review board accepts protests through May 15, or through the 30th day after delivery of your notice when that falls later. Notices for single-family homesteads are mailed around April 1, and the board starts hearing protests around mid May.

If the board's decision does not satisfy you, the Comptroller lists district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000. An owner who appeals still has to pay at least the undisputed tax before the delinquency date, so a protest does not pause the bill.

sections.h2: How are Tyler property taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, and the owner on that date is liable for the year's tax. Your sale contract decides how the year's bill is split between buyer and seller at closing.

If you sell mid-year, ask the Smith County Tax Office for the amount due before closing and get the payoff figure in writing. A homestead exemption does not transfer on its own: a buyer who closes after January 1 may claim it for the rest of that year if the seller did not receive it, and heirs without a recorded deed must file an affidavit of ownership interest and the owner's death certificate.

faqs.q: What is the City of Tyler property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of Tyler lists $0.242063 for 2026-2027, and Smith County's table shows the same figure as the adopted 2026 rate. Your full bill also includes county, junior college and school district rates.

faqs.q: Where do Tyler homeowners pay their tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Smith County Tax Office at 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, or call (903) 590-2920. The county office collects for all taxing jurisdictions in Smith County, including the City of Tyler.

faqs.q: When do Tyler property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1 for most bills. State rules call for payment by January 31, and unpaid tax on February 1 picks up a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

faqs.q: Is every Tyler address in Tyler ISD?
faqs.a: No. The city notes that some properties inside Tyler are in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD. Check your tax statement to see which school district rate applies.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Tyler?
faqs.a: School districts must give $140,000 off a residence homestead's value, plus $60,000 more for seniors or disabled owners. Local exemption amounts for the city and county are a question for the Smith County Appraisal District.
